title: Sheriff Cuellar Meets Governor-elect Hinojosa to Talk Operation Lone Star, Public Safety
excerpt: Webb County Sheriff Martin Cuellar met with Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa and fellow border sheriffs on Wednesday to discuss Operation Lone Star and public safety, sharing a white paper on the technology and strategies Webb County uses — and pushing to keep the program funded statewide.
content:
Webb County Sheriff Martin Cuellar met with Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa and fellow border sheriffs on Wednesday, November 19, to discuss Operation Lone Star and public safety, the Sheriff’s Office announced.

Cuellar said he was grateful for the chance to share Webb County’s border security efforts and to talk about ways to strengthen law enforcement capabilities across Texas.

Cuellar also prepared a white paper laying out the technology, equipment and strategies Webb County uses in its border security operations, according to the Sheriff’s Office. What began as a border security initiative has grown to cover school safety — including threats such as active-shooter incidents — and severe weather monitoring to better protect local communities, he said.

His goal, Cuellar said, is for Webb County’s model to serve as a blueprint not only along the border but throughout Texas. He is advocating for continued Operation Lone Star funding so sheriff’s offices statewide can be equipped with the same advanced technology Webb County uses, along with additional deputies on the ground.

“Together, these resources will serve as a force multiplier, strengthening our ability to respond to threats and protect lives,” Cuellar said.

Hinojosa defeated Gov. Greg Abbott in the November 3 election and will become Texas’ first Latina governor when she takes office on January 19, 2027.

Sources: Webb County Sheriff’s Office, Nov. 19, 2026; Associated Press, Nov. 3, 2026.
